text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Key Hebron issue still unresolved. Jordan's King Hussein making first visit to territories since 1967.
- Israeli President Ezer Weizman says his visit improves ties with Egypt. Egypt rolls out red carpet.
- Health Minister Tsahi Hanegbi hopes DNA testing will solve mystery of missing Yemeni children.
- Israeli cabinet: Rethink Brodett Committee proposals to tax interest on short- and mid-term savings.
- Experts panel to propose alternatives to Brodett's recommendations. Tel Aviv Stock Exchange unaffected by cabinet vote.
- Lockheed bid to buy TAAS's heavy munitions division, the most profitable of the government company's businesses.
- Central bank, government, industrialists move toward rate-cut consensus.
- Economy will suffer if peace process fails to get back on track, says head of international marketing of securities at Bank Hapoalim.
GLOBES

- Finance Minister Dan Meridor: Taxation of savings to be resubmitted to government. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu: I see no reason the finance minister cannot continue in his job. Assessment: Meridor won't quit.
HAARETZ
- King Hussein lands this morning in Jericho and will visit autonomous areas for first time since 1967.
- By a majority of 4-2 the government rejects the tax recommendation on savings plans.

- Restraining orders may be issued against right-wing activists ahead of the Hebron redeployment. National Religious Party to convene in the city at month's end, after the prime minister agreed to appear.
- Reform Jewish donors won't contribute to United Jewish Appeal because of "discrimination against their people in Israel".
- C&W: We are interested in increasing control over Bezeq Telecommunications.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Aides to Meridor say he will have a hard time staying in the job if he is hit again. Experts expect committee will "bury" the Brodett report.
- Former Mossad man in Canada who disclosed secrets says he hopes it wasn't "them" who were behind a fire at his house.
MAARIV
- "Agreement on Hebron -- soon," say Israeli sources.
- Secret plan in prime minister's office to lower taxes by 2-3 percent.
